correctness.rationale: The source Hamiltonian gives the nonlinear-gradient coefficient proportional to 1-1/p. Mass-preserving scaling and the stationary virial identity yield the exact kappa=2 identity H(lambda)-H(1)=H2(lambda^2-1)^2, proving the p>1/p=1/p<1 trichotomy. A separate sech-integral calculation gives the first-order critical-power displacement 3 epsilon_NR (p-1)/(p+1). Claims are limited to Derrick scaling of the truncated nonrelativistic Hamiltonian.

originality.rationale: The claim is restricted to the source-specific SS+(1/p)VV interpolation. Prior work already contains pure SS/VV corrections and general nonlinear-Dirac stability caveats; those are not claimed as new. Searches found no SCOPE overlap or public correction of arXiv:2609.18170 deriving the exact p=1 sign switch, square scale-energy identity, or interpolating first-order threshold.

value.rationale: The result corrects the source's blanket positivity assumption for H2 on 0<p<1, replaces it with an exact critical-power scale classification, and quantifies the p-dependent displacement of the Derrick threshold on both sides of p=1.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
